name: Agri World
description: A world primarily dedicated to producing food, livestock, fibres or other agricultural resources for export.

name: Civilised World
description: A broadly developed and self-sustaining Imperial world that does not fall into a more specialised primary class.

name: Dead World
description: A lifeless or effectively uninhabitable world, often stripped, sterilised or ruined by ancient catastrophe.

name: Death World
description: A world whose climate, geology, fauna, flora or other hazards make ordinary human survival exceptionally difficult.

name: Cemetery World
description: A world devoted largely to tombs, mausoleums, battle graves and the ritual care of the dead.

name: Hive World
description: A massively populated world whose inhabitants are concentrated in immense, layered hive cities.

name: Feudal World
description: A low-technology world whose societies are commonly organised around hereditary lords, warrior elites and agrarian domains.

name: Research Station
description: A world, moon or installation primarily assigned to sanctioned scientific, medical or technological research.

name: Forge World
description: A Mechanicus-ruled industrial world dedicated to manufacturing, resource processing and the maintenance of sacred technology.

name: Feral World
description: A human world whose dominant cultures remain tribal, nomadic or otherwise technologically primitive.

name: Abattoir World
description: A world dedicated to the mass breeding, slaughter and processing of animals or other edible biomass.

name: Adepta Sororitas Sanctuary World
description: A world serving as a protected religious, conventual or operational sanctuary of the Adepta Sororitas.

name: Adeptus Astartes Breeding World
description: A controlled population world used to cultivate physically suitable human stock for future Space Marine recruitment.
notes: Rare and morally extreme; most closely associated with the Death Spectres.

name: Adeptus Astartes Fief World
description: A world held as part of a Space Marine Chapter's protected domain or feudal territory.

name: Adeptus Astartes Homeworld
description: The principal planetary base of a Space Marine Chapter and usually the site of its fortress-monastery.

name: Adeptus Astartes Recruiting World
description: A world from whose population a Space Marine Chapter regularly selects aspirants.

name: Adeptus Mechanicus World
description: A world controlled or dominated by the Adeptus Mechanicus without necessarily meeting the full definition of a Forge World.

name: Administratum World
description: A world devoted primarily to bureaucracy, records, taxation, logistics and the administration of Imperial territory.

name: Anchor World
description: A fortified fleet-support and logistics world used to sustain major Imperial war fronts or naval corridors.

name: Arboreal World
description: A world covered by cultivated or natural forests and exploited primarily for timber, resins or other arboreal resources.

name: Archeotech World
description: A world notable for extensive remains of ancient human technology, especially relics from the Dark Age of Technology.

name: Archive World
description: A world dedicated to preserving historical, legal, military or administrative records.

name: Armoury World
description: A world used to manufacture, maintain or stockpile vast quantities of weapons, armour and military materiel.

name: Astropathic Relay Station
description: A planetary or orbital node used to receive, amplify and retransmit astropathic communications.

name: Battery World
description: A world dedicated to generating, storing or exporting immense quantities of usable energy.

name: Capital World
description: The administrative capital of a political territory, system, sub-sector or other Imperial jurisdiction.

name: Cardinal World
description: A major centre of Ecclesiarchal authority ruled or overseen by a powerful cardinal.

name: Colony World
description: A recently established or still-developing Imperial settlement world.

name: Fortress World
description: A planet transformed into a heavily defended military bastion guarding a vital route, border or objective.

name: Frontier World
description: A sparsely developed Imperial world at the edge of controlled or well-charted space.

name: Garden World
description: A pleasant, lightly industrialised world valued for natural beauty, agriculture or elite habitation.
notes: Often overlaps with Paradise World; terminology varies by source.

name: Garrison World
description: A world maintained chiefly as a permanent military base, troop depot or defensive occupation point.

name: Hub-Fortress World
description: A major fortified command and logistics hub linking multiple war zones, routes or subordinate strongholds.

name: Industrial World
description: A heavily industrialised world focused on manufacturing but not necessarily governed by the Adeptus Mechanicus.

name: Knight World
description: A usually feudal world ruled by noble houses that maintain and pilot Imperial Knights.

name: Labyrinth World
description: A world dominated by immense mazes of ruins, tunnels, urban structures or natural passages.

name: Linchpin Planet
description: A strategically indispensable world whose loss could destabilise an entire region, campaign or defensive network.

name: Lumber World
description: A world whose primary tithe or export is timber and related biological materials.

name: Menagerie World
description: A world used as a planetary-scale preserve, zoo or containment site for rare and dangerous creatures.

name: Merchant World
description: A major commercial centre dominated by trade houses, markets, finance and interstellar commerce.

name: Mining World
description: A world primarily exploited for ores, minerals, promethium or other subterranean resources.

name: Munition World
description: A world dedicated to producing ammunition, explosives and other expendable war materiel.

name: Paradise World
description: An unusually safe, beautiful and comfortable world often reserved for elites, recreation or prestigious settlement.

name: Penal World
description: A prison world used for incarceration, forced labour, punishment and sometimes the raising of penal military units.

name: Penitent World
description: A deliberately austere or dangerous world where inhabitants live in imposed or voluntary religious penance.

name: Port World
description: A world whose economy and strategic value centre on voidship traffic, docking, cargo handling and transit.

name: Quarantined World
description: A world isolated by Imperial decree because of disease, mutation, xenos presence, corruption or another severe hazard.

name: Quarry World
description: A world stripped for stone, aggregate and surface-accessible construction materials.

name: Ratling World
description: A world predominantly inhabited by Ratlings or associated with Ratling abhuman populations.

name: Refugee World
description: A world used to receive and house populations displaced by war, invasion or planetary disaster.

name: Relic World
description: A world valued for sacred, historical or technological relics and the sites associated with them.

name: Repository World
description: A world serving as a secure storehouse for records, relics, supplies, specimens or strategic reserves.

name: Salvage World
description: A world whose economy revolves around recovering useful material and technology from ruins, wrecks or battlefields.

name: Scribe World
description: A bureaucratic world populated by scribes and devoted to copying, processing or preserving Imperial records.

name: Scriptorum World
description: A world organised around vast scriptoria that copy, illuminate, catalogue or reproduce texts and records.

name: Sector Capital World
description: The principal administrative and political capital of an Imperial sector.

name: Sentinel World
description: A watch-world or bastion positioned to detect and resist threats approaching a strategically important region.

name: Sepulchre World
description: A world dominated by vast tomb complexes, sacred memorials and funerary institutions.

name: Shadow World
description: An obscurely classified world associated with secrecy, concealment or exceptional strategic sensitivity.
notes: Usage is source-specific rather than a common Administratum standard.

name: Shrine World
description: A major pilgrimage world centred on a saint, miracle, holy relic or sacred event.

name: Spoil World
description: A world used as a dumping ground for mining spoil, industrial debris and other planetary-scale waste.

name: Tallow World
description: A world dedicated to rendering fats and producing candles, oils and related materials for Imperial use.

name: War World
description: A world trapped in prolonged, large-scale or effectively permanent warfare.

name: Warden Planet
description: A guarded world tasked with watching, containing or protecting a dangerous region, object or route.

name: Waste World
description: A world ruined or dominated by pollution, barren wastes, refuse and ecological devastation.

name: Abandoned World
description: A previously inhabited world whose population and active settlements have been deserted.

name: Artificial World
description: A constructed planetary-scale body or habitat rather than a naturally formed world.

name: Asteroid
description: A minor rocky body that may be inhabited, fortified, mined or classified like a world.

name: Cavern World
description: A world whose major habitats or ecosystems exist in extensive underground caverns.

name: Chem World
description: A world whose atmosphere, oceans or surface are dominated by hazardous industrial or natural chemicals.

name: Crystal World
description: A world notable for vast crystalline formations, mineral structures or crystal-dominated geology.

name: Derelict World
description: A world with abandoned infrastructure, ruins or installations that remain physically present but non-functional.

name: Desert World
description: A world dominated by arid deserts and extreme scarcity of surface water.

name: Forest World
description: A world covered predominantly by forests rather than dense tropical jungle.

name: Gas Giant
description: A massive gaseous planet that may host orbital settlements, floating habitats or valuable atmospheric resources.

name: Ghost World
description: An apparently empty, dead or abandoned world whose true status or surviving inhabitants may be uncertain.

name: Husk World
description: A stripped, scorched or hollowed planetary remnant with little remaining life or usable material.

name: Ice World
description: A world dominated by glaciers, frozen oceans, snowfields or extreme cold.

name: Jungle World
description: A world covered predominantly by dense, planet-spanning jungle.

name: Lava World
description: A geologically violent world with widespread lava seas, volcanic plains or exposed magma.

name: Membrane World
description: A world displaced through the Warp and deposited into a star system by an anomalous membrane-like translation event.

name: Molten World
description: A world whose surface is largely molten because of extreme heat, tidal stress or geological catastrophe.

name: Mountain World
description: A world dominated by extreme mountain ranges, high plateaus and rugged terrain.

name: Nomad World
description: A rogue planet travelling through interstellar space without orbiting a normal star.

name: Ocean World
description: A world whose surface is almost entirely covered by oceans.

name: Planetoid
description: A planetary or near-planetary body smaller or less conventionally formed than a standard planet.

name: Rad-soaked Planet
description: A world saturated by dangerous radiation from war, stellar conditions, industry or natural deposits.

name: Scrapworld
description: A world covered in scrap, wreckage and discarded technology, often supporting scavenger societies.

name: Swamp World
description: A world dominated by wetlands, marshes, bogs and waterlogged terrain.

name: Unclassified World
description: A world that lacks a reliable official classification or whose nature remains uncertain.

name: Wreck Graveyard
description: A planetary, orbital or deep-space region containing immense concentrations of derelict vessels and wreckage.

name: Cache World
description: A hidden world used to store laboratories, experiments, clones, specimens or other secret assets.

name: Daemon World
description: A world consumed or reshaped by the Warp and ruled by daemonic or Chaos powers.

name: Fallen Knight World
description: A Knight World whose ruling houses have fallen to Chaos or become renegades.

name: Hell Forge
description: A Chaos-controlled industrial world or stronghold manufacturing daemon engines, weapons and corrupted technology.

name: Heretic Astartes Fief World
description: A world held as territory or a vassal domain by a Chaos Space Marine warband or Legion.

name: Heretic Astartes Recruiting World
description: A world exploited by Chaos Space Marines for recruits, slaves, cultists or potential aspirants.

name: Craftworld
description: A vast, self-contained Aeldari world-ship carrying an entire civilisation through space.

name: Crone World
description: A former heartland world of the ancient Aeldari empire, now usually within the Eye of Terror and saturated by Chaos.

name: Exodite World
description: A world settled by Aeldari Exodites who maintain austere, low-technology societies bound to the planet's world spirit.

name: Hold World
description: A major Kin-held world organised around a Votannic Hold and its associated civilisation.

name: Kin World
description: A world inhabited, claimed or controlled by the Kin of the Leagues of Votann.

name: Larder World
description: A Tyranid-controlled world where biomass is preserved or cultivated for later consumption.

name: Maiden World
description: A paradise world terraformed by the ancient Aeldari as a future colony or refuge.

name: Necron Tomb World
description: A world containing dormant or awakened Necron tomb complexes and dynastic infrastructure.

name: Ork World
description: A world dominated by Orks and reshaped by their settlements, industry, warfare and spores.

name: Squat Homeworld
description: A traditional stronghold or homeworld of the old Squat civilisation.
notes: Older setting terminology; modern Leagues of Votann sources more commonly use Kin and Holds.

name: T'au World
description: A world incorporated into or controlled by the T'au Empire.

name: T'au Sept
description: A principal T'au world and its surrounding territory, forming a major cultural and administrative sept.

name: Xenos World
description: A world dominated, inhabited or controlled by a non-human species.

name: Other World
description: A catch-all category for worlds that do not fit the established indexed classifications.

name: Moon
description: A natural satellite that may receive the same functional and environmental classifications as a planet.

name: Pleasure World
description: A leisure-focused world serving as a resort, retreat or playground for wealthy and powerful Imperial citizens.
notes: Often treated as an alias or close relative of Paradise or Garden World.
